host.name: Reverse GitOps
host.description: The manifesto, FAQ, talks, and known implementations for Reverse GitOps: an API-first operating model where users and agents submit validated intent through a typed Kubernetes API, and a controller records that intent back into Git as declarative YAML.

entries.description: The full manifesto: why requiring every change to enter through Git strains, and the three principles — API first, capture intent not implementation, GitOps still applies — along with the explicit non-goals.
representativeQueries: API-first alternative to pushing YAML to Git
write Kubernetes API changes back into Git automatically

entries.description: Answers to the common objections: why not use Git directly, whether this replaces GitOps, how it relates to application configuration, and where the pattern does not fit.
representativeQueries: why not just let developers edit Git directly

entries.description: Open-source projects implementing the pattern, including gitops-reverser — a Kubernetes operator that captures API activity via audit webhooks and commits sanitised, intent-only YAML to Git with the real actor as commit author.
representativeQueries: Kubernetes operator that writes API changes to Git
